descriptor: Magnetic and current-sensing components maker building alloys, relays and rare-earth magnets
lede: A 65-year-old Mumbai maker of magnetic and current-sensing parts (shunts and current transformers for electricity meters, sensors and assemblies for EVs and cars) that is adding specialty alloys, relays and, through a subsidiary, rare-earth magnets. H1 FY27 revenue grew 32% at a ~21% EBITDA margin on EV demand, and management raised its FY27 margin outlook to 20-25%; but alloys, relays and magnets all slipped again in October, and PML's stake in the magnet subsidiary is to fall to about half.

short_version.text: Q2 FY27 revenue +49% to ₹72 Cr with a 24.6% EBITDA margin on EV and smart-meter demand; H1 FY27 +32%. FY27 guidance: 20-30% growth, margin raised to 20-25% (from 15-18%). FY26 guidance was met, and the rare-earth Phase 2 lines were commissioned in October, on time, with a 25% ECMS capex incentive approved.

Relays slipped three times (FY26 → H2 FY27 → ramp-up FY28); alloys cut to ₹40-50 Cr for FY27 after furnace breakdowns (with delay penalties); magnet revenue pushed to FY28. EV demand has orders for H2 only. Consolidated debt rose from ₹24 Cr to ₹92 Cr for subsidiary capex, return on new capital was negative over FY24-26, and a 2015 winding-up order is still only stayed in court.
~40x trailing earnings and ~17x EV/EBITDA, against Mishra Dhatu at 50x, Pricol at 29x and HPL Electric at 15x.

blocks.text: PML designs customer-specific magnetic sensing, current sensing, magnetic assemblies, alloys and ZAMAK die-cast parts. It is often the only supplier for a product, selling to tier-1 auto companies (ICE and EV) and top electricity-meter makers worldwide. Its wholly owned subsidiary Quantum Magnetics is localising NdFeB rare-earth magnets in phases, from assemblies to block cutting and machining, then powder-to-block.

blocks.text: The core business has met its numbers; the new businesses have not met their dates. An investor on the May 2026 call called the last two years of execution 'a very poor show', and the MD agreed relays started much later than expected.

items.text: Promoters hold 58.1%, steady for a year; no pledge.
Institutions hold almost nothing; ~17,500 shareholders, falling.
Auditors' emphasis of matter: a 2015 Bombay High Court winding-up order (on a freight forwarder's petition) is stayed but still pending; ₹0.19 Cr deposited.
No key audit matters; no related-party transactions flagged as material.
The MD's pay rose 28% to 34 times the median employee.
PML lent ₹2.73 Cr to and guaranteed ₹0.83 Cr for Quantum Magnetics in FY26.
PML's stake in Quantum Magnetics is to fall to 49-50%; terms of the new shareholder not disclosed on the call.

blocks.text: Scenarios are illustrative, built on our assumptions, not company guidance.

PML's core business is profitable, cash-generative and growing again, and H1 FY27 is ahead of guidance. The valuation leans on alloys, relays and rare-earth magnets, which have repeatedly started late and are funded with rising debt. Relay pilot supplies, customer approvals for magnets and whether H2 keeps the EV-led margin are the things to watch.
